findings.title: Expired cache entries are reported as active cache
findings.body: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds groups all CalendarCache rows for the credentials without filtering on expiresAt. getCachedAvailability treats rows with expiresAt in the past as cache misses, but this method will still return their updatedAt, so the UI displays an expired, unusable cache as present and offers to delete it. Filter to unexpired rows (expiresAt >= now) when computing status.

findings.title: Deleting cache does not refresh the connected-calendars query
findings.body: deleteCacheMutation only shows a toast and calls the optional onSuccess prop; unlike disconnectMutation below it never invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars. In SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper onChanged is optional and often undefined, so after a successful deletion the dropdown keeps showing the old cacheUpdatedAt timestamp and 'Delete cached data' action until a manual refetch, contradicting the success toast.

findings.title: Handler bypasses the calendar-cache disabled/mock repository selection
findings.body: The handler directly instantiates the concrete CalendarCacheRepository instead of going through the CalendarCache factory used elsewhere (CalendarCache.init), which returns CalendarCacheRepositoryMock returning [] when calendar-cache is disabled. When the feature is disabled, this endpoint will still query CalendarCache and surface cache status/deletion for leftover rows that the rest of the system intentionally ignores.

findings.title: Cache deletion ignores disableConnectionModification gating
findings.body: canDisconnect respects delegationCredentialId and disableConnectionModification, but hasCache is computed only from integration type and cacheUpdatedAt, and the early return is `if (!canDisconnect && !hasCache)`. On screens that set disableConnectionModification to make the connection read-only/managed, a Google credential with cache still renders the dropdown and enables the destructive delete-cache mutation, defeating the flag that hides disconnect in the same UI.

findings.title: Every cache refresh rewrites all SelectedCalendar rows via an empty update
findings.body: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache now calls SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(credential.id, {}) on every cache population. That performs a write touching updatedAt for every SelectedCalendar row of the credential (including event-type-scoped rows), so updatedAt no longer reflects user selection changes, adds a DB write to a hot availability path, and is not even used by the new UI, which displays CalendarCache.updatedAt via cacheUpdatedAt.

findings.title: Ownership failure is thrown as a generic 500 error
findings.body: When the credential does not exist or does not belong to the caller, the handler throws a plain Error('Credential not found or access denied'). tRPC will surface this as INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR rather than a client error such as TRPCError with NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN, polluting server-error monitoring and giving API consumers the wrong contract for an expected authorization outcome.

findings.title: No tests for the new cache-status query or ownership-checked deletion
findings.body: The PR adds a new authenticated mutation that deletes data based on credential ownership, a groupBy status query, and a mock implementation, but adds no tests. There is no coverage that another user's credentialId is rejected, that only the caller's credential cache is deleted, or that getCacheStatusByCredentialIds returns the latest updatedAt per credential, so an authorization or mapping regression would ship undetected.

findings.title: Committed tunnelmole helper is macOS-only, cwd-dependent, and masks failures
findings.body: `sed -i ''` is BSD/macOS syntax and fails under GNU sed on Linux; ENV_FILE='../.env' resolves relative to the caller's working directory rather than the script/repo root, so running it from the repo root writes ../.env outside the repo; and cleanup() always exits 0, so the failure paths at the tunnel-URL check report success to callers. This unrelated dev script should be fixed or removed from the feature PR.

findings.title: dev:cron now depends on unpinned, undeclared tsx via npx
findings.body: The script changes `ts-node cron-tester.ts` (ts-node is a declared devDependency) to `npx tsx cron-tester.ts`, but tsx is not declared anywhere in the workspace dependencies. Running the script will download an unpinned package at runtime, failing offline and introducing version/supply-chain drift; it is also unrelated to the calendar-cache feature. Add tsx as a devDependency or keep ts-node.

findings.title: Cache timestamp is always formatted with the en-US locale
findings.body: The cache_last_updated timestamp is formatted with `new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', ...)` regardless of the user's locale from useLocale. Non-English users will see US date/time formatting in an otherwise localized UI; format with the active locale instead.
